```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = NA)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

bayesplot::bayesplot_theme_set(ggplot2::theme_gray())
bayesplot::color_scheme_set(scheme = "brightblue")
```

In this vignette we present all available options for the choice of the prior and Monte Carlo rule in `housepi`. 
Parameter definitions are associated as shown in the [Walkthrough](walkthrough.html).

To perform the sampling we consider the "blank" model, i. e. a data independent template model, with loglikelihood always equal to zero.

```{r, eval = TRUE}
# create an instance of the blank model
blank_model <- housepi::HouseholdModel$new("blank")
```

# Continuos Priors

Here's the full list of available continuous distributions present in `housepi`:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
# continuous distributions in housepi
available_distrs <- c("unif", "norm", "lnorm", "gamma", 
                      "weibull", "rayleigh","beta", "exp")

# add a parameter definition for each available distribution
for (distr in available_distrs) {
  blank_model$add_param(name = distr, prior = distr)
}
```

Here we associated definitions of parameters to infer with default arguments and default proposer rules (Gibbs sampling). 
 
```{r}
# perform the sampling with the inference command
# note: since loglikelihood is 0, posterior and prior sampling are equal
blank_model$infer(progress = FALSE)
```

The warning just reminds us that we are using a dummy model.

```{r, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
# density plot of the traces (w\o loglikelihood)
bayesplot::mcmc_dens(blank_model$traces_no_loglike)
```

## Provide a Custom Range

```{r}
# add list of parameter definitions
# option 'append = FALSE' drop previous definitions
blank_model$load_param_list(
  default = list(prior = "norm"),
  below = list(prior = "norm", min = -1),
  above = list(prior = "norm", max = 1),
  both = list(prior = "norm", min = -1, max = 1)
)
blank_model$infer(progress = FALSE)
```

```{r, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
bayesplot::mcmc_dens(blank_model$traces_no_loglike)
```

# Discrete Priors

```{r, include=FALSE}
bayesplot::color_scheme_set(scheme = "orange")
```

Here's the full list of available discrete distributions present in `housepi`:

```{r}
# discrete distributions in housepi
discrete_distrs <- c("pois", "binom", "nbinom", "geom")
blank_model$drop_all()
for (distr in discrete_distrs) {
  blank_model$add_param(name = distr, prior = distr)
}

# perform the sampling 
blank_model$infer(progress = FALSE)
```

```{r, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
# plot the histograms
bayesplot::mcmc_hist(blank_model$traces_no_loglike, binwidth = 1)
```

## How to Discretize Continuos Priors

Previous continuous priors can be chosen to be discretized simply by adding the flag `discrete = TRUE`.

```{r}
# drop all current definitions
blank_model$drop_all()

# add a parameter definition for each available distribution
for (distr in available_distrs[available_distrs != "beta"]) {
  blank_model$add_param(name = distr, prior = distr, discrete = TRUE)
}

# perform the sampling 
blank_model$infer(progress = FALSE)
``` 

```{r, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
# plot the histograms
bayesplot::mcmc_hist(blank_model$traces_no_loglike, binwidth = 1)
```

# MCMC Proposer Rules

```{r, include=FALSE}
bayesplot::color_scheme_set(scheme = "purple")
```

```{r}
blank_model$drop_all()

# available proposer rules in housepi
available_proposer_rules <- c("gibbs", "unif", "norm", "lnorm")

# add a parameter definition for each available proposer rule
for (rule in available_proposer_rules) {
  blank_model$add_param(name = paste("rule", rule), prior = "norm", 
                        min = 0, rule = rule, scale = 0.1)
}

blank_model$infer(progress = FALSE, n_steps = 100)
```

```{r, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
bayesplot::mcmc_trace(blank_model$traces_no_loglike)
```
Note that the proposer rule "lnorm" does not fit the case of negative values.

### Role of Finite Adaptation

```{r, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}

blank_model$infer(progress = FALSE, n_steps = 100, n_adapt = 1000)

bayesplot::mcmc_trace(blank_model$traces_no_loglike)
```
